To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Learners’ constructional representations are primed by the same constructions that native speakers use, and that they can be sorted into the same semantic space as the native speaker constructions”.

(a) German learners of English exhibit a significant construction-based priming effect, (b) this effect is not based on syntactic priming, and (c) it correlates strongly with verb-construction associations in native speaker corporas.

(1) the constructional status of the verb-construction pairings in non-native speakers’ grammars can be shown to be (2) constructionally rather than syntactically determined and (3) that these constructional verb-construction pair- ings can be shown to reflect the native-speaker constructional preferences.
